questions.question: What happens when you press Run on a program?
questions.code:
print("Hello!")
# Press Run to execute the program.

options.text: The computer starts executing the program's instructions.
The computer permanently saves every value in the program.
The computer automatically fixes every mistake in the code.
The computer turns the program into a physical device.

questions.explanation_correct:
EXCELLENT!
Running a program means the computer begins executing the instructions in that program.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Not quite!
Run starts execution. It does not automatically fix mistakes or turn the program into hardware.

questions.question: Why does a running program need memory?
questions.code:
score = 100
name = "Alex"
# Values must be kept track of while the program runs.

options.text: To keep track of values and information the program is currently using.
To make the monitor display a larger image.
To replace the computer's processor.
To automatically write missing lines of code.

questions.explanation_correct:
SPOT ON!
A running program needs memory to keep track of values and information it is working with.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Try Again!
Memory is used to hold information the running program needs; it does not replace the processor or write code for you.

questions.question: In this code, what does the variable score represent while the program is running?

options.text: A name used to refer to the value 100.
A command that permanently stores 100 on the hard drive.
A breakpoint that pauses the program.
A programming language used to run the code.

questions.explanation_correct:
NICE!
The variable name score refers to the value 100 in the running program.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Not quite!
score is a variable name referring to the value 100; it is not a breakpoint, language, or disk command.

questions.question: What is a bug in a program?
questions.code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
total = price + quantity
# We intended a different calculation.

options.text: A problem that makes a program behave differently from what was intended.
A special command that makes programs run faster.
A type of computer memory used for storing variables.
A button used to start a program.

questions.explanation_correct:
CORRECT!
A bug is a problem in a program that causes its behavior to differ from what the programmer intended.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Try Again!
A bug is a problem in the program's behavior, not a command, memory type, or Run button.

questions.question: What is debugging?
questions.code:
# Find out why the result is wrong
print("Investigate!")

options.text: Finding and understanding problems in a program.
Making a computer physically faster.
Deleting every variable from memory.
Writing code without ever running it.

questions.explanation_correct:
GREAT JOB!
Debugging is the process of finding and understanding bugs so you can fix the program.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Not quite!
Debugging is about investigating problems in code and understanding why the program behaves incorrectly.

questions.question: What does a breakpoint do?
questions.code:
score = 100
name = "Alex"
print(score)
# Imagine placing a breakpoint on print(score)

options.text: It pauses the program at a chosen point so you can inspect what is happening.
It permanently deletes the line where it is placed.
It automatically changes incorrect code into correct code.
It makes every instruction run at the same time.

questions.explanation_correct:
SPOT ON!
A breakpoint pauses execution at a chosen point, giving you a chance to look at the program's current state.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Try Again!
A breakpoint is for pausing execution so you can investigate. It does not delete or rewrite code.

questions.question: Why would you step through a program while debugging?
questions.code:
a = 5
b = 10
c = a + b
print(c)
# Step through these lines one at a time.

options.text: To watch the program execute one small part at a time.
To skip all of the program's instructions.
To permanently stop the program from running.
To automatically remove all bugs.

questions.explanation_correct:
NICE!
Stepping lets you execute the program one piece at a time and observe what changes.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Not quite!
Stepping is a way to observe execution gradually. It does not skip everything, permanently stop the program, or automatically fix bugs.

questions.question: What can you learn by inspecting variables while a program is paused?
questions.code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
total = 13
# The debugger shows the current values.

options.text: What values the program currently has in memory.
What the programmer will write in the future.
How much electricity the monitor is using.
Which programming language will be invented next.

questions.explanation_correct:
MODULE COMPLETE!
Inspecting variables lets you see the values the program currently has while it is paused.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Almost!
Variable inspection is useful because it shows the program's current state and the values it is working with.
